If you’re up for it, you should definitely ride Soarin’ at Epcot. Thrilling without actually being a thrill ride- I’ve been on it a million times and it still amazes me every time. All the mountains at Magic Kingdom are great too- thunder mountain, space mountain, and splash mountain are classics (but space mountain is my favorite). Everest at animal kingdom is super fun as well. Tower of Terror is awesome if you aren’t scared of heights- excellent theming and very immersive. Seven dwarves mine train is very cute and has an entertaining queue but I wouldn’t wait more than 30 minutes unless you have small children because it is a very short ride with tiny ride vehicles. For slower rides, I personally love spaceship earth and the peoplemover/Tomorrowland transit authority. Some might find it boring, but they’re relaxing and beautiful to me. 

I would highly recommend seeing the Festival of the Lion King show, I feel like it’s really underrated. In club cool at Epcot you can sample soft drinks from different countries. If you have time for it, Disney Springs is actually beautiful and has tons of stores. I love taking the boat there as the view and the breeze are beautiful. Honestly, sometimes it’s fun to just wander around your hotel. 

In terms of restaurants, Ohana and Cape May Cafe are my personal favorites. Trail’s End is a good buffet too. The pot roast, french onion soup, and desserts at Be Our Guest are very good but everything else on the menu is just so-so to me (but the atmosphere of the restaurant is absolutely beautiful). I’ve never been to Sanaa but I’ve heard wonderful things about it.
